hcontainer.name: item
hcontainer.heading: Action in relation to enrolments on State and Northern Territory Rolls

content.p: (1) This item applies if, immediately before the commencement time, a person’s name is on the Roll (the old Roll) for a Division in a State or the Northern Territory because of subsection 95AA(2) or (3) of the Commonwealth Electoral Act 1918 (as in force immediately before the commencement time).
The Electoral Commissioner must:
transfer the person’s name by:
deleting the person’s name from the old Roll; and

(ii) deleting the annotation made under section 95AC of the Commonwealth Electoral Act 1918 (as in force immediately before the commencement time) in respect of the person’s name from the old Roll; and

(iii) entering the person’s name and other particulars required by section 83 of the Commonwealth Electoral Act 1918 on the Roll (the new Roll) for the Division in the Australian Capital Territory that does not include the Jervis Bay Territory; and
notify the person in writing of the actions taken under paragraph (a).
However, if the Electoral Commissioner is satisfied that the person is not entitled to be enrolled on the new Roll:
subitem (2) does not apply; and

(b) the Electoral Commissioner must delete the annotation made under section 95AC of the Commonwealth Electoral Act 1918 (as in force immediately before the commencement time) in respect of the person’s name from the old Roll; and

if the rules require or permit the Electoral Commissioner to take specified action in relation to the person’s enrolment, the Electoral Commissioner must or may (as the case may be) take that action; and
the Electoral Commissioner must notify the person in writing of:
the action taken under paragraph (b); and
any action taken under paragraph (c).
Despite subitem (2), the Electoral Commissioner must not take an action under paragraph (2)(a) within a period:
starting at 8 pm on the day of the close of the new Roll for an election to be held in the Division in the Australian Capital Territory that does not include the Jervis Bay Territory; and
ending on the close of the poll for the election.
Despite subitem (3), the Electoral Commissioner must not take an action under paragraph (3)(b) or (c) in relation to a Roll for a Division within a period:
starting at 8 pm on the day of the close of the Roll for an election to be held in the Division; and
ending on the close of the poll for the election.

section.heading: Application of Commonwealth Acts

content.p: An Act or a provision of an Act extends to the Territory of its own force except so far as the Act or another Act expressly provides otherwise.
Except as provided by this Act, an enactment has no effect so far as it purports to affect the application of an Act or a provision of an Act in or in relation to the Territory.

create an offence or civil penalty;
provide powers of:
arrest or detention; or
entry, search or seizure;
impose a tax;
set an amount to be appropriated from the Consolidated Revenue Fund under an appropriation in this Act;

(4) Subsection 12(2) (retrospective application of legislative instruments) of the Legislation Act 2003 does not apply to transitional rules made before 1 July 2017.

If the operation of this Schedule or the transitional rules would result in an acquisition of property (within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxxi) of the Constitution) from a person otherwise than on just terms (within the meaning of that paragraph), the Commonwealth is liable to pay a reasonable amount of compensation to the person.

If the Commonwealth and the person do not agree on the amount of the compensation, the person may institute proceedings in a court of competent jurisdiction for the recovery from the Commonwealth of such reasonable amount of compensation as the court determines.
This Schedule has no effect to the extent (if any) to which it imposes taxation.
This Division does not, by implication, limit the matters that may be dealt with by Ordinances under section 19A of the Norfolk Island Act 1979.
